title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that identical candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we produced N = 250 intent pairs with gpt-5-mini and ran two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation calls + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed; the confirmatory estimand reported here applies to the synthetic/emulation partition only. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived and referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps) because they can synthesize device CLI sequences from operator intents. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk (syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties) that motivates deterministic verification or human oversight [1],[2].

Architectural response and gap. A common architectural response is generate–verify–repair (GVR): generate a candidate, run a deterministic validator, and—if necessary—attempt bounded automated repair before acceptance [3],[4]. Prior work shows GVR reduces mechanically checkable defect classes, but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of validator+repair when modern LLMs already produce candidates conforming to validator encodings under constrained tasks.

Research question and contributions. We ask: when the same initial LLM candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics), what is the marginal verifier-detected difference in intent-satisfaction between accepting the candidate and running a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment that preserves shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate the validator/repair marginal effect; (2) artifact-grounded numeric results and deterministic reconciliation showing event-level model-call accounting; and (3) a concise discussion of interpretive limits and reproducibility.
sections.related_work:
LLM-driven configuration: Surveys and recent NetOps studies show LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups but often require verification or human review for production safety [1],[2],[5].

Deterministic verification and GVR: Deterministic validators and header-space or model-based checks are mature for many forwarding/policy properties and are used as validators in research GVR pipelines; generate-and-verify and repair workflows reduce mechanically verifiable errors but do not by themselves resolve deeper semantic correctness or cross-vendor subtleties [3],[4],[6].

Security and injection risks: Prompt-injection and indirect-injection threats on LLM-integrated applications motivate filtering and validator layers; adaptive adversaries and retrieval attacks remain open evaluation challenges [7].

Positioning: Unlike prior work that mixes generation variability across conditions, our preregistered paired design enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics so the only permitted source of paired difference is deterministic validation and the single automated repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). The confirmatory design is paired (N_pairs = 250) with generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Analysis plan: exact two-sided McNemar and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), implemented by the registered paired_binary_analysis_v1.

Explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting (required clarification). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent; that identical candidate was used for both baseline and guarded episodes. Provider-accounting reconciles to hosted_model_call_event_count = 251, decomposed into 250 shared_initial_generation calls plus 1 repair call (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json records stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 251). Adapter labels observed in the audit (e.g., condition_counts = {"shared": 250, "guarded": 1}) reflect the adapter's internal event categorization and should be interpreted via the stage_counts mapping: the adapter records the shared initial generation under the "shared" label and the single repair generation under the repair stage; this manuscript's paired estimand compares baseline acceptance of the shared candidate to guarded validation (and permitted repair) of the same candidate.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced 250 constrained intent tasks. Each task payload encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, protected interfaces, and a difficulty label. Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break switchover, atomic MTU changes, safe access transfer patterns). The full task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl).

Model, validator, and guarded pipeline. The declared model for initial generations was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which implements full_intent_constraint_validation: parsing CLI, checking required_sequence and workflow constraints, constructing an expected_final_state snapshot, and emitting a binary valid flag plus diagnostic fields (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). When validator.valid == false, the pipeline permitted up to one automated repair attempt drawn from deterministic repair templates (syntactic reordering, command-splitting/joining, and ordering corrections) and re-ran the validator once. No multi-iteration repairs, retrieval augmentation, or human escalation were permitted in the confirmatory protocol.

Inclusion, contamination, and missingness. Pre-registered exclusion rules remove trials with vendor-parser-blocking syntax preventing deterministic verification or trials containing credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors flag instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items are excluded from primary analysis per preregistered rules. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged (complete_pair_count = 250; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty).

Confirmatory analysis details. Primary test = exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes (baseline vs guarded). Paired difference CI computed by paired-bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). All analysis artifacts (contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap parameters) are archived and referenced.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256: 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9). Deterministic reconciliation reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 251 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) yields p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0.0–1.2 percentage points). Bootstrap parameters and results are archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair trace. Validator traces for passed episodes show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count and valid = true. Representative artifacts include execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json (parsed_command_count = 6, required_command_count = 6, valid = true) and corresponding guarded artifacts. A single repair trace (the only repair call) converted the failing baseline candidate into a guarded pass; the repair trace and resulting guarded scoring artifact are archived in raw_results.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near‑null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of adding deterministic validation plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the lone failing candidate. The upper bound of the paired-bootstrap CI (1.2 percentage points) quantifies the maximum verifier-detected improvement consistent with these data.

Why the effect is small (artifact-grounded). Artifact evidence points to three factors: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduce ambiguity and favor well-formed CLI sequences (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl); (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced syntactically well-formed, policy-aligned sequences for these constrained tasks (raw responses archived); and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state snapshot) and does not capture broader runtime or cross-device emergent correctness.

Power and preregistration assumptions. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline pass ≈ 0.90 and targeted detection of a 15 percentage-point effect with N_pairs = 250. The realized baseline pass-rate (0.996) exceeded that assumption and consequently reduces power to detect small absolute improvements; the paired-bootstrap CI is therefore the more informative practical summary.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: results are sensitive to prompt templates, the single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct validity: the validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not dynamic protocol-level safety. External validity: confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition (the preregistered sim-to-real contrast was not executed). Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not tested.

Operational implications (bounded). In tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM a single-repair guarded validator may yield only a small marginal verifier-detected improvement. This empirical bound does not imply validators are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts; richer validators, multi-iteration repair, human escalation, or production heterogeneity could materially change the benefit calculus.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the marginal verifier-detected effect of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intents, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate with the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). The preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed; results apply only to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced here are archived and available as described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and key artifacts (concise): declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Representative archived manifest and analysis pointer: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256: 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9). The full execution and analysis manifest, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and artifact-hash manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by the manifest above. No human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.

Deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, expected_final_state) but did not assess dynamic protocol-level behavior or emergent cross-device correctness.
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive adversarial and retrieval-based prompt-injection attacks, and large-scale production heterogeneity, were not exercised and remain open threats.
